html:
Milarepa was a Tibetan yogi and poet, one of the most loved figures of Tibetan Buddhism. He is usually dated 1052 to 1135.

His life story is famous. After his father died, an uncle and aunt seized the family's land and made Milarepa and his mother servants. His mother had him learn black magic for revenge, and he is said to have killed dozens of people by bringing down a house on a wedding party. Later, full of remorse, he sought out the teacher Marpa the Translator.

Marpa tested him harshly for years, making him build stone towers and then tear them down. Only then did he teach him. Milarepa spent the rest of his life meditating alone in mountain caves, wearing only a thin cotton cloth.

  • He sang his teachings in songs, later gathered as The Hundred Thousand Songs of Milarepa.
  • His disciple Gampopa founded the monastic tradition of the Kagyu school.

His biography, written by Tsangnyön Heruka in 1488, is still one of the most read books in Tibet. He lived in the same revival of Buddhism that followed Atisha's arrival.
sum: Milarepa was a Tibetan yogi and poet, one of the most loved figures of Tibetan Buddhism. He is usually dated 1052 to 1135.
